3106: The School of Undergraduate Studies is a key component of IIM Bangalore’s broader vision to contribute to undergraduate education in India with the same academic rigour and global orientation that characterize its postgraduate offerings. The campus is located approximately 23 kilometres from IIMB’s Bannerghatta Road campus and is being developed as a dedicated residential academic environment designed to foster interdisciplinary learning, research and innovation. The School will initially offer two four-year, full-time residential programmes: BSc (Hons) in Data Sciences with a minor in Economics, and a BSc (Hons) in Economics with a minor in Data Sciences. The inaugural cohort comprises 80 students, with 40 students in each programme.

3108: The second panel discussion on, ‘Jal Jeevan Mission: From Pipeline to Policy – Ensuring Sustainability Beyond Har Ghar Jal’ was moderated by Prof. Gopal Naik, Chairperson, Senior Fellow and Jal Jeevan Mission Chair Professor at the Centre for Public Policy, IIM Bangalore. The discussion brought together perspectives from Shri Parameswaran Iyer, former Executive Director, World Bank and former Secretary, Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS); Liby T Johnson, Executive Director, Gram Vikas; Fouzia Taranum, Commissioner, RDWSD, Government of Karnataka; Anuj Sharma, Chief Executive Officer, Arghyam, Bengaluru, and Jafar Shareef Sutar, Deputy Secretary (Admin.), Rural Drinking Water and Sanitation Department (RDWSD), Government of Karnataka.
3109: The second panel on the ‘Education’ track, moderated by Prof. Mukta Kulkarni, Dean, Programmes, IIMB, with Anand Gautam, EkStep Foundation; Ayushi Khare, Indus Action; Prof. Dwarika Prasad Uniyal, RV University; and Harnam Shankar, RightWalk Foundation, shifted the focus towards using DPI and AI to improve scale, access, quality and inclusion in education. The speakers argued that digital academic records must be accompanied by opportunities, scholarships and institutional support that move with the learner, not just the records themselves, while cautioning that legacy government systems, privacy concerns and institutional differences continue to complicate true interoperability. "India needs a kind of revolution to create scale, access and value, a triangle that is very difficult to achieve in higher education," said Prof. Uniyal.

3114: The strategic collaboration builds on IIT Kanpur’s strengths in science, engineering, research and technology development, supported by its state-of-the-art R&D infrastructure.
